API1:2023.name: Broken Object Level Authorization
API1:2023.description: APIs expose endpoints that allow users to access objects without proper authorization checks.
API1:2023.recommendation: Enforce object-level authorization on every request.

API2:2023.name: Broken Authentication
API2:2023.description: Authentication mechanisms are improperly implemented, allowing attackers to compromise accounts or tokens.
API2:2023.recommendation: Implement strong authentication, MFA, secure session management, and robust JWT validation.

API3:2023.name: Broken Object Property Level Authorization
API3:2023.description: APIs expose or modify object properties that users should not be able to access.
API3:2023.recommendation: Validate authorization for every property before returning or updating data.

API4:2023.name: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
API4:2023.description: Lack of limits allows attackers to exhaust server resources through excessive requests or payloads.
API4:2023.recommendation: Implement rate limiting, request throttling, quotas, and payload size restrictions.

API5:2023.name: Broken Function Level Authorization
API5:2023.description: Users can invoke administrative or privileged API functions without proper authorization.
API5:2023.recommendation: Perform role-based access control checks for every API endpoint.

API6:2023.name: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
API6:2023.description: Sensitive business processes can be abused because business logic protections are missing.
API6:2023.recommendation: Implement anti-automation controls, rate limits, and business logic validation.

API7:2023.name: Server Side Request Forgery
API7:2023.description: The API fetches remote resources based on user-controlled input.
API7:2023.recommendation: Validate destination URLs, use allowlists, and restrict outbound network access.

API8:2023.name: Security Misconfiguration
API8:2023.description: Improper configuration exposes APIs to unnecessary risk.
API8:2023.recommendation: Disable unnecessary features, apply secure defaults, configure security headers, and harden servers.

API9:2023.name: Improper Inventory Management
API9:2023.description: Undocumented, deprecated, or forgotten API versions remain accessible.
API9:2023.recommendation: Maintain an accurate API inventory and retire obsolete endpoints.

API10:2023.name: Unsafe Consumption of APIs
API10:2023.description: Applications trust third-party APIs without sufficient validation or security controls.
API10:2023.recommendation: Validate responses, authenticate third-party APIs, and verify integrity before processing data.
